co_overlook_cliff.blurb: Overlook Cliff is a steep bolted crag perched above the Ouray Ice Park, with open views over town and up the Uncompahgre canyon. Nearly all of the climbing is sport, and the grades cluster in the 5.11 and 5.12 range, so it suits climbers comfortable on sustained, overhanging lines rather than beginners. Out of Pocket, Overlooked and 99 Problems are among the best-regarded lines. The hike up is short but the terrain is steep and the cliff is ringed by smaller bands, so follow the path rather than heading straight at the wall.
co_overlook_cliff.parking_note: Drive south out of Ouray on US 550 and bear right after the first switchback, toward Yankee Boy Basin and Camp Bird Road. Pull off on the right about four-tenths of a mile along, across from the Sutton Mine trail sign.
co_overlook_cliff.approach: Hike the Sutton Mine Trail about half a mile to the overlook, then turn right on a faint path along the ridgeline to the cliff base. Reach the routes by coming onto the ledge from its left end.

co_north_chasm_view_wall.blurb: North Chasm View Wall is a big gneiss face on the north rim of the Black Canyon of the Gunnison, reached by dropping into the canyon rather than walking up to it. The routes are long, mostly traditional, and range from about 5.9 up through hard 5.12 and a few 5.13 lines, with the 5.12 climbs forming the largest group. Expect runouts, route-finding and variable rock; this is committed adventure climbing where rescue is slow. The wall tends to feel warmer and brighter than the walls across the canyon. The Free Nose and The Scenic Cruise are two of the better-known lines. Poison ivy and ticks can be a nuisance below.
co_north_chasm_view_wall.approach: Almost everyone descends Cruise Gully, entered at a sign on the rim between the campground and the ranger station. It steps down through two rappel sections, often with fixed lines already in place, and lets out on bushy talus at the foot of the wall.

co_maxwell_falls.blurb: Maxwell Falls sits in the pine forest west of Evergreen, where granite boulders and outcrops line the trail up to a small waterfall. The climbing here is mostly bouldering, with problems running from easy up into the V9 and V10 range, plus a handful of sport and top-rope lines on the cliffs. Fat Lady and Cowboy Love are two of the harder boulder lines, and John's Own Stone is the sport route most worth knowing. Plan on a real hike with crash pads, since the boulders are spread along the trail rather than gathered at one spot, and the trail through the rocky cliff section can be hard to follow.
co_maxwell_falls.parking_note: From Evergreen, head south on CO 73, then turn right (west) onto South Brook Forest Road. The lower trailhead lot is on the left after about three and a half miles and is easy to drive past; the upper trailhead is a bit farther along as the road becomes Black Mountain Drive.

co_sheep_s_nose.blurb: Sheep's Nose is a large granite dome beside the road in the West Creek valley, the first formation you meet on the right. It rises roughly 600 feet and holds cracks, corners and knobby faces, with climbs from one to five pitches long, nearly all of them traditional. Most grades sit between 5.8 and 5.11, with the 5.9 range especially well represented. Lost in Space Direct and Chinook are popular choices on the south side. West Creek is quieter than much of the South Platte, but the road is poor in winter, so it is mainly a spring through fall destination.
co_sheep_s_nose.parking_note: After turning onto the West Creek road, go roughly half a mile to a pullout on the right, below the dome, where there is a gap in the fence.

co_mural_wall.blurb: The Mural Wall is one of the three cliffs that make up the Gallery at Shelf Road, a long, clean face of limestone that is best known for hard sport climbing in the 5.12 range. Motif, The Mural and Montage are good examples, but there is also a solid supply of 5.10 and 5.11 lines for climbers working up to them. The wall faces southwest and gets shade in the morning, which makes it more comfortable on warm days than much of Shelf. As elsewhere at Shelf, the rock is sharp and pocketed, and trad is a poor fit because it is brittle.

co_fern_canyon_bouldering.blurb: These boulders are scattered across a steep, wooded hillside in the southern Flatirons above Boulder. Some stand around 30 feet tall, and the rock ranges from quite good on some blocks to crumbly on others. A few of the boulders are tall enough to be rope-climbed along the Fern Canyon trail. Problems run from VB-V1 up to around V10 on this hillside, with most falling in the V2 to V7 range. Because the slope is forested, the boulders stay cool on hot summer days. Bring pads for a long uphill carry, as the walk in is substantial and the terrain is uneven.

co_lower_animal_world.blurb: Lower Animal World is the lowest of the three tiers at Animal World in Boulder Canyon, a short walk above the highway. Mostly bolted one-pitch sport routes of roughly 40 to 100 feet, with a handful of moderate cracks mixed in. Grades run from the 5.7 range up to hard 5.12, and the 5.11 and 5.12 routes together make up about half of what is here. Piles of Trials and Threshold Of A Dream are two of the better 5.11 and 5.12 lines. It sees more traffic than the tiers above it, and loose rock on the approach and ledges above the road is a real hazard to anyone below.
co_lower_animal_world.parking_note: Use the large pullout on the left about 8.5 miles up Boulder Canyon, just past a long sweeping right bend; it is shared with the Boulderado cliff.

co_grazing_allotment_crag.blurb: Grazing Allotment is a granite crag in the Red Feather Lakes country of northern Colorado, a region of granite domes and pine forest. Both bolted sport lines and traditional crack and corner routes are found here, in a mix that runs from 5.8 through hard 5.12, with the bulk in the 5.10 to 5.12 range. Steve the Duck, Shadow Battle and Talon Scout are among the highlights, and Joyride and Pythagorean Rhythm give good options a notch easier. It is a long drive from the Front Range towns, so most people make a full day of it.
co_grazing_allotment_crag.parking_note: From Red Feather Lakes, follow County Road 67J to Prairie Divide Road; the crag's parking is on the right roughly five miles along that dirt road.

co_whale_s_tail_the.blurb: The Whale's Tail is a small sandstone outcrop inside Eldorado Canyon State Park, tucked beside the trail near Redgarden Wall and facing the Bastille. It packs a broad spread of difficulty into a compact space: low-angle slabs around 5.2 to 5.5 that make a gentle introduction to the canyon, and steeper lines through 5.12 that are often top-roped. Nearly all the climbing is traditional, and NED (Nothing Except Dynamics) is the hardest named line here. The canyon rock is known for demanding, removable-gear craft, so even short climbs deserve care.
co_whale_s_tail_the.approach: Cross the bridge and follow the trail; the outcrop is just off it to the west, beside Redgarden Wall and opposite the Bastille.
